name: WebGPU adapter info
plain: Asks the browser which GPU vendor and architecture WebGPU will run on.
meaning: Returns vendor, architecture and sometimes device and driver description, a cleaner GPU label than WebGL's masked string. Chrome rounds it, but features and limits still expose the hardware tier.

limits.headline: Can ask which graphics maker and design your device will use for 3D work
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page uses WebGPU
can: Get the graphics maker and chip design name
Sometimes get a device or driver description
Tell phone, laptop and desktop graphics apart
cannot: Get the exact model in Chrome, which rounds the answer
Work in browsers without WebGPU support
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge round the label. Safari and Firefox have limited or newer support for WebGPU.

story.what_it_is: A page asks the browser which GPU vendor and architecture WebGPU will use.

marketing.name: WebGPU
marketing.pitch: Chrome describes WebGPU as a modern way to use the graphics chip for fast games and graphics on the web.

marketing.name: WebGPU API
marketing.pitch: Gives pages high performance access to the graphics chip for drawing and for general computing.

story.for_you: You see faster 3D scenes and some AI features running in the tab. The page can also see what kind of graphics chip you have, and it does not ask you.
story.for_makers: Game engines and AI in the browser pick the best settings by chip type. Browsers limit the detail they give out, because the same data is a strong fingerprint.

use_cases.example: A browser game using a modern engine picks high or low quality by the GPU family, so it runs smoothly.
Figma and other design tools move to WebGPU for faster drawing of huge files.
A web app that runs an AI model on your device checks the GPU before choosing a model size.
A web video editor uses the GPU to apply effects while you preview.
A game studio gathers GPU families from visitors to see which graphics chips need a fix.
A fraud engine notices a server GPU in a login that claims to be a laptop.
A tracker adds the GPU vendor and architecture to a device ID.

technical_bounds: Needs a GPU the browser has allowed
Chrome may return empty device and description
No user prompt but blocked in some privacy modes

value.legit_uses: Pick compute backend and model sizes
value.abuse: Adds GPU-class signal, sidesteps WebGL masking

history.change: WebGPU ships on Windows, macOS, ChromeOS
WebGPU in Safari, iOS and visionOS
